_about: Lane B. Newspoll quarterly/replica demographic breakdown tables (The Australian, aggregated pooled releases by state, gender, age, metro) covering each election's final fieldwork window, 2013–2022. Reality check from the Poll Bludger WP archive: the quarterly breakdown product only exists for some of the election quarters — 2013 (Jul–Sep) never ran because of the campaign/election cycle, 2016 ran as two mid-campaign 'breakdowns of the last three/four polls' releases (May + late June 2016), 2019 (Apr–Jun) never ran (post-failure poll pause; next quarterly was Nov–Dec 2019), 2022's last breakdowns piece was the Jan–Mar 2022 quarterly (published 25 Mar 2022) plus the 20 May 2022 election-eve poll's national figures. Poll Bludger posts relayed the figures in prose — no HTML tables anywhere in these posts — and are saved verbatim under src/newspoll/.

fragments: …state-level federal voting intention results… Labor with a lead of 54-46 in New South Wales (out from 53-47 in the last quarter of 2021); 58-42 in Victoria (out from 56-44); 53-47 in Western Australia (in from 55-45) and 59-41 in South Australia (out from 55-45), but with the Coalition leading 54-46 in Queensland (unchanged). [pollbludger.net 2022-03-25]

Labor now leads 60-40 among the 35-49s, up from 54-46; is at 50-50 among the 50-64s, after trailing 53-47 last time; and has narrowed the gap among the 65-plus cohort from 60-40 to 58-42. Conversely, the Coalition's deficit among the 18-34s narrows from 69-31 to 66-34. [same post]

Labor also now leads among all four income cohorts, including a 55-45 lead among those on $150,000 and above, after trailing 53-47 last time. The poll records no gender gap on two-party preferred, with Labor's lead among men widening from 52-48 to 55-45 among men and 54-46 to 55-45 among women. [same post]
waves.note: All figures are two-party-preferred as relayed; the printed piece also carried primary-vote tables which were not relayed in the post and were not captured this pass (paywall + IA offline). Income cohort labels beyond '$150,000 and above' not printed in the relay.

notes: PRODUCT TIMELINE (from the full Poll Bludger WP index, saved searches 'quarterly'/'breakdowns'/'aggregates'): Newspoll quarterly breakdown posts exist at 2012-12-29, 2013-04-01, then a 2013-12-28 post covering Oct–Dec 2013 ('four post-election polls… total samples ranging from 554 in SA to 1352 in NSW'); 2015 onwards quarterly-ish (2015-04-06, 2015-12-28, 2016-03-28 'January-March 2016', 2016-10-03 'August-September 2016', 2017-04-11 'February-March 2017', 2017-10-09, 2018-07-09 'state breakdowns', 2018-12-26, 2019-03-26, 2019-12-26 'November-December 2019', 2020 (May/June-Aug/Nov-Dec), 2021 QVA Jan-Mar/Apr-Jun/Jul-Sep/Dec, 2022-03-25 (Jan–Mar 2022), 2022-12-26 ('July to December' aggregate).

Quarterly tables in this product print primary vote AND 2PP by STATE, GENDER, AGE (bands 18–34/35–49/50–64/65+ in the 2022 vintage; 2013–2016 banding '18-34/…' per era), and METRO/city vs non-city; 2022 vintage added income cohorts. Only the relayed fragments above are captured verbatim; the full matrices sit behind The Australian's paywall and in Wayback — archive.org was offline ('Temporarily Offline') for this whole pass so no archived article/PDF could be fetched.

GhostWhoVotes (the era's verbatim-tables mirror, cited by Poll Bludger's 2013 Q4 post) is gone: ghostwhovotes.wordpress.com holds only a 2010 'Inactive' post (WordPress REST found:1), and the tables moved to Twitter screenshots, unscrapeable headlessly. theaustraliannewscorpau.files.wordpress.com → wordpress.com blog is DELETED (410).

Blind filename probes on the OPEN origin CDN origin.theaustralian.com.au/wp-content/uploads/<YYYY>/<MM>/newspoll.pdf all 404 for 2013/10, 2016/05, 2016/06, 2016/10, 2019/03, 2019/07, 2022/03, 2022/05(Newspoll.pdf too), 2022/06 — Newspoll PDF uploads of the modern 'Newspoll (pooled)' kind do not exist for these waves (matches the auto-skill's note that only SOME 2025-26 pooled waves have PDFs).

2016 mid-campaign Newspoll breakdowns cadence detail: (a) published ~29–30 May 2016 pool = 'last four Newspoll surveys going back to the start of April' (Newspoll was fortnightly: fieldwork windows approx 31 Mar–3 Apr, 14–17 Apr, 28 Apr–1 May, 12–15 May); (b) published ~27–28 June 2016 pool = 'the last three Newspoll surveys'. Exact fieldwork spans could not be pinned from the open relay text — dateStart/date left approximate (date = approximate publication date).
Row-sum self-checks: Jan–Mar 2022 age/state/gender rows are 2PP pairs summing 100; 2022-05 national row sums 91 printed (rest unprinted). No row exceeded 100.5.

Consolidated 2026-11-10: the 2013 election-eve card, the 2016 June-pool table PDF and the scanned Jan–Mar 2019 quarterly PDF all recovered from Wayback (News Corp assets host + files.wordpress.com mirror). June-2016 superseded two relay-fragment waves; Q1-2019 remains flagged adjacentQuarter; the 2019 pre-election record = Q1 table + 14-May state-breakdowns pool.
gaps: 2013-09-07 election: NO Jul–Sep 2013 Newspoll quarterly exists. Probed: Poll Bludger WP index Oct–Nov 2013 (2013-09-10→2013-11-20 listing shows only per-poll Newspoll posts + state one-offs NSW/Vic), the 2013-12-28 post itself ('four post-election polls' = Oct–Dec pool), GhostWhoVotes (dead), origin-CDN PDF probes (404). The era's quarterly cadence shows Q2 and Q3 2013 were both skipped (campaign + election). Nothing more exists to find.

2016-07-02 election: the PRINTED full tables (primary+2PP by state; June piece's gender/age/metro cells) — only fragmentary swings survive in open relays; needs Wayback captures of the ~30 May and ~28 June 2016 Australian articles (IA offline this pass) or screenshot sources.

2019-05-18 election: NO Apr–Jun 2019 quarterly exists — Newspoll (YouGov Galaxy) paused after its 2019 miss; the first post-election breakdown product was 'November-December 2019' (relayed 2019-12-26, post-election, out of scope). Nearest preceding quarterly = Jan–Mar 2019, filed above as adjacentQuarter. Campaign-era state breakouts were not published (checked Poll Bludger Apr–Jul 2019 'quarterly'/'breakdowns'/'aggregates' result sets, all read in full text).
